title: Saghtekoos / Appletree Neck
summary: Saghtekoos is recorded as a neck of land in Islip, known in English records as Appletree Neck.
history_content: The name appears in a 1692 license to Stephen Van Cortlandt to purchase Saghtekoos and in a 1697 patent for a neck bounded by Oak Neck Brook, an Indian footpath, and Saghtekoos Creek.
translation_content:
Saghtekoos is treated as probably the name of the Indigenous owner or resident of the neck. The name is compared with words for a snake, adder, or rattlesnake, and the possessive form is visible in Saghtekoo's.

Why Place Names Matter

“Names are more than just how we refer to a place. They centre a history and shape our perception of where we live.”

— Rhiannon Russell, The Original North (2021), Article text
preservation_content: Saghtekoos preserves a Native personal or place-name within the Islip shoreline now remembered through Appletree Neck and Sagtikos-area names.
